internal_consistency_issues.detail: All 117 sold lots have a winner in the 10 valid 2022 franchises and a non-null final_price. All bid_steps price ladders are non-decreasing. No final_price falls below its last stated bid_step. No violations found.

spot_check_15_lots.method: 15 random lots cross-read against raw HTML narration (seed=2022)
spot_check_15_lots.result: All 15 matched the raw HTML on outcome, winner and (for sold lots) price. Confirmed examples: Alex Hales->KKR 1.5cr ('Sold for 1.5 crore'), Quinton de Kock->LSG 6.75cr, Wanindu Hasaranga->RCB 10.75cr, Krunal Pandya->LSG 8.25cr, T Natarajan->SRH 4cr, Mohammad Arshad Khan->MI 0.2cr; unsold/re-entry rows (Sameer Rizvi, Ben McDermott, Aproov Wankhade) matched 'Unsold'/'No bids' narration.

notes: Accuracy: of 117 ESPN sold lots, 92 overlap with the independent Wikipedia sold table and ALL 92 agree on BOTH winning team AND final price (0 price mismatches, 0 winner mismatches). No contradictions between the two independent sources on any shared player.
No corrections were applied: the spec requires a correction be confirmed wrong by BOTH the raw HTML and the independent source, and there were zero confirmed errors.

Two apparent 'winner mismatches' surfaced by fuzzy name-matching were investigated and dismissed as false matches: ESPN 'Mohammad Arshad Khan' (MI, 0.2cr) was spuriously paired with Wikipedia 'M. Shahrukh Khan' (PBKS, 9.0cr), and ESPN 'Ashok Sharma' (KKR, 0.55cr) with 'Abhishek Sharma' (SRH, 6.5cr). Both ESPN players are confirmed in the raw HTML and are simply absent from Wikipedia's table; they are different people, not data errors.

Coverage: the ESPN blog is a HIGHLIGHTS live blog and narrates only ~117 of the ~204 players actually sold. Wikipedia's parsed 'Sold players' table is itself incomplete (133 rows). The 25 only-in-ESPN and 41 only-in-source entries are coverage gaps in one source or the other, each verified against its own origin; none indicate an error in the audited file.

Internal consistency is clean: valid winners, all sold lots priced, non-decreasing bid_steps, final_price >= last bid_step. The only duplicate (player, outcome) rows are 19 UNSOLD re-entries (accelerated rounds), which the spec explicitly permits.
Hammer-vs-paid / retention adjustments: none needed. All 92 overlapping prices matched exactly, so no price gap had to be reconciled via the overseas pay-cap or retention-cost rule.
No change was made to 2022_bids.json; schema preserved as-is.
